Subject: quick question from Tangle

Hi Abi, saw pi-freeflow has an AGENTS.md. I'm on Tangle Sandbox, which runs untrusted agent tasks in isolated Linux machines; shell, files, ports, desktop and trace come through an SDK and CLI. Is giving agents their own machine something you'd ever want for projects like this, or does your current setup cover it? Either way, thanks for reading.

If an agent is about to run code you didn't write, the first question is where that code runs.

Sandbox's answer: its own isolated Linux machine, for every untrusted agent task. Through the SDK or CLI, the agent works with shell, files, ports and a desktop, and you get a trace of what it did. When a task goes sideways, read the trace, throw the machine away, run the next one.

Isolation is the first product decision in agent infrastructure. Make it on purpose.

https://sandbox.tangle.tools/

Model routing tends to collapse into one of two extremes: everything automatic, or a routing config you maintain by hand.

Router takes a middle position. One API for model inference, managed providers by default. When you want a specific call to go somewhere specific, you set an explicit operator route, and the decision stays yours where it matters.

If your code already speaks the OpenAI SDK, it already speaks Router.

https://router.tangle.tools/

Most agent tools are good at drafts. The unsolved part is everything after the draft.

GTM Agent is a workspace for a founder: give the agent your product and a sales goal, connect your tools, and set its authority. It researches and it drafts. Then the draft waits in review, and nothing sends until you authorize it.

Draft and send are different states, and the agent can't cross that line alone. That boundary is what makes handing over real work survivable.

https://gtm.tangle.tools/

An agent you never tested in private will test itself in public.

Agent Builder creates domain agents; you set the personality, the instructions and the tools. The feature that decides whether this goes well: profiles can stay private. Keep one private, run it against real tasks, fix what it gets wrong, publish when it stops embarrassing you.

Testing before publication is how an agent earns its instructions.

https://agents.tangle.tools/
